sample_unit: patients (NCCT scans) in external validation cohorts; 8 physician readers in reader study
models_evaluated: machine learning based LVO detection algorithm on non-contrast CT

links.outcome: Clinician diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance, including automation bias
links.effect: AI assistance increased pooled AUC from 0.718 to 0.852, sensitivity from 46.6% to 63.7%, and specificity from 91.9% to 94.9% (all P<0.001); automation bias reliance-level BHR 9.25.
links.quote: AI assistance significantly increased pooled AUC values from 0.718 to 0.852, sensitivity from 46.6% to 63.7%, and specificity from 91.9% to 94.9% (all P<0.001).

links.outcome: Standalone AI performance on independent external multinational cohorts
links.effect: AUC 0.963 (95% CI 0.946 to 0.975) in Korean cohort and 0.899 (95% CI 0.858 to 0.939) in US cohort.
links.quote: Standalone AI achieved AUC values of 0.963 (95% CI 0.946 to 0.975) in the Korean cohort and 0.899 (95% CI 0.858 to 0.939) in the US cohort.

screen.reason: Evaluates clinician diagnostic performance with vs. without AI assistance in a multi-reader multi-case study, including an analysis of automation bias.
